core_obligations: Reduce to one class: for odd n the centre of the spin group has order two, so the author's remark shows that there is only one Tits algebra to consider (proof line 639).
Identify it: that Tits algebra is Brauer equivalent to the even Clifford algebra of the matrix over the field, by the cited computation (proof line 640).

Read off the criterion: the single Brauer class is split over Q exactly in the first alternative and non-split over R exactly in the second, and combining the two alternatives with the division-algebra description of universality gives the stated equivalence (proof line 640).
proof_roadmap: 由 n 为奇数时 spin 群中心为 2 阶，只需考虑一个 Tits 代数。
该 Tits 代数与原矩阵的偶 Clifford 代数 Brauer 等价，于是 Q 上分裂 或 R 上不分裂 这两个择一条件正好对应 R-universality。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the R-universality criterion for an odd-dimensional special orthogonal Lie algebra (author prop at source lines 632-636): universality holds exactly when the even Clifford algebra of the symmetric matrix splits over Q or fails to split over R. The proof (source lines 638-641) is short and reduces the whole criterion to a single Brauer class: the oddness of n makes the centre of the spin group of order two, so only one Tits algebra occurs, and that algebra is Brauer equivalent to the even Clifford algebra, whose splitting behaviour over the two fields is exactly the stated alternative. The card keeps the author's own level of detail. H2.
